short_answer: Payne Insider is a real, long running pick service. The same Payne co hosts Bet The Board, a free NFL and college football betting podcast with former oddsmaker Todd Fuhrman, which moved to Clay Travis's Sport & State in 2026. He does not publish his last name, and the site gives no company name, address or phone number, only an email address.

The site sells football packages, but on 16 Nov 2026 no price appeared in the page text; buying runs through a PayPal button. The terms say all sales are final and that nothing about performance is guaranteed.

The records page is more open than most: it lists every season since 2007 by sport, including losing years such as 2019 to 2020 football at minus 34.44 units and 2024 to 2025 football at minus 7.51 units. It is still the seller's own tally, with no individual picks, dates or odds we could check. We found no independent buyer reviews at all, positive or negative.
pricing_intro: We read the football picks page on 16 Nov 2026. It says "2026 Football Packages Available Now" but shows no package names or prices in its text. The order button is a PayPal hosted button, and the PayPal payment page did not show an item or price to us. We do not guess prices.
pricing: Price not shown in the page text
PayPal checkout; terms say all sales are final, no refunds
guarantee: There is no guarantee. The terms carry the heading "All Sales Are Final" with "No Refunds", and say the payment counts as fully earned once you get into the members area. No refund is due if a package ends early for any reason.
The terms also say the advice "is not guaranteed in terms of any type of performance." Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually much larger than the package price.

claims_note: The years do not line up neatly. The homepage says 16 years, the football page counts 19 football seasons, and the records page dates the public service to 2007, which is 19 or 20 seasons ago.

To the seller's credit, the records page lists losing seasons as well as winning ones. We counted two losing football combo seasons in recent years (2019 to 2020 and 2024 to 2025) and several losing sport splits in older years, such as 2013 to 2014 NBA. That is more than most pick sellers show.

Units are counted in "DIMES" on a 1 to 10 confidence scale, with an average play of about 2.2. Without the individual picks, the odds taken and the time each was sent, a buyer cannot rebuild these totals or check the claim about beating the closing line.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. There is no pick by pick log with lines, odds and release times, and we found no third party tracker that has graded the paid plays.

What the seller publishes: season totals by sport from 2007 onward. Recent football combo seasons run from 51% (2019 to 2020, minus 34.44 units) to 60.8% (2022 to 2023, plus 69.69 units). The current 2026 to 2027 line read 38 wins, 31 losses and 1 push on 16 Nov 2026.
TheRX forum keeps a list of services whose write ups members should not repost, and PayneInsider was on it in February 2026. That tells us the paid plays circulate, but not how they perform.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Payne Insider pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Payne Insider performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the seller's football claims sit at 51% to 61% in recent seasons. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Payne Insider is almost nonexistent. The only buyer comments we found sit on the seller's own testimonials page. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no independent buyer posts about Payne Insider on CapperTek, in Reddit through the Arctic Shift archive, or in TheRX and Sportsbook Review searches. The only customer voices are 25 undated testimonials chosen by the seller, all positive, praising steady profits, discipline and plays that move lines. There is no pattern of complaints, but there is also no independent praise, so buyers have very little outside evidence either way.

The testimonials page shows 25 notes signed with a first name and a place or job title, none dated. They describe winning months and seasons, renewals, and plays that move the betting line, and two are credited to Las Vegas oddsmakers. The seller picks what appears here, so it is not independent evidence.

CapperTek lists PayneInsider.com as an unverified service with no reviews or complaints. A TheRX search found the name only in the forum's list of services whose write ups should not be reposted, with no comments on results.

A post search of r/sportsbook, r/sportsbetting and r/SportsBettingPicks in the Arctic Shift Reddit archive found no thread about the service. Comment searches for the name timed out on the archive side, so Reddit comments were not fully checked.

conflicts: Payne co hosts Bet The Board, a free podcast whose new home on Sport & State has Hard Rock Bet as presenting sponsor, according to Awful Announcing. A sportsbook sponsor of the free show is a financial tie a buyer should know about, though it says nothing about the paid picks.
We saw no sportsbook links or affiliate banners on the payneinsider.com pages we read.
strengths: A long running service that publishes season by season totals since 2007, and shows losing seasons as well as winning ones.
The seller has a public face through a podcast with a known former oddsmaker.
Terms are written out plainly, including the no refund rule.
concerns: No price appears in the page text before checkout.
All sales are final. No refund and no guarantee of any kind.
No pick by pick record, so the season totals and the closing line claim cannot be checked.
The operator gives no last name, company name, address or phone number, only an email address.
No independent buyer reviews exist that we could find; the only customer comments are seller chosen testimonials.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. Season totals are not a record you can check.
Count units, not wins. Ask what one DIME means in dollars before you size bets off it.
Read the terms before you pay: all sales are final here.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real service that has sold football picks since at least 2007, run by the same Payne who co hosts the Bet The Board podcast. We could not verify that the picks win over time, because only season totals are published, and we found no independent buyer reviews, complaints, or court or regulator action.
How much does Payne Insider cost?
On 16 Nov 2026 the football picks page showed no prices in its text. Checkout runs through PayPal, and the terms say all sales are final with no refunds.
Does Payne Insider have a verified record?
No. The records page lists season totals by sport since 2007, including losing seasons, but no individual picks, dates or odds. Nobody independent has graded the paid plays that we could find.

You get a long running football service whose own numbers show more winning seasons than losing ones. What is unproven is whether a buyer betting at the lines they can actually get beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110, and nothing refunds the package or your betting losses.
